Hi Sara — answers inline below, and attaching the SLA PDFs for your legal team to review. Happy to have Neha jump in with more technical detail (she’s copied).

Q1 — "30 days to remove from live store": this is our standard operational SLA for tenant-level deletion requests once a verified deletion request is received and scheduled. It’s a committed operational timeline (we include it in our standard contract language). Verification: deletion jobs are tracked and we can provide audit evidence (delete job id + timestamp) under a compliance request.

Q2 — Backups/snapshots (90-day purge default): by default we retain backups/snapshots up to 90 days to support disaster recovery; backups are encrypted at rest using customer-keyed KMS where requested. Backups are logically isolated per tenant and purged as part of the deletion workflow. If you require a shorter backup retention window (e.g., 30 days) we can support that via a contractual option (small operational fee and rollout window).

Q3 — Log retention: default audit/access log retention is 180 days. Logs are stored separately from primary data; critical security logs are retained for 180 days by default and included in backup rotation only as metadata (not full payload). We can scope a shorter log retention window on request; note that reducing log retention may affect forensic capability.

Additional notes: SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA. We also provide a standard DPA with GDPR terms and a BAA for HIPAA — both available in the legal packet (link in attachments).

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-slas.pdf, redwood-log-retention-appendix.pdf

Would you like us to start the vendor questionnaire now? We can either: 1) receive the spreadsheet and mark answers, 2) provide a CSV export of our security portal answers, or 3) grant temporary read-only access to our security portal (preferred for speed).

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Technical clarifications: backups, snapshots, and log deletion workflow

Hi Sara — quick technical follow-up to Marissa’s notes. Details below so your engineers/compliance folks have the specifics they asked for:

- Live deletion workflow: when a tenant data deletion request is triggered we run a multi-step purge: mark records for deletion -> wipe indexes and KV caches -> remove objects from primary object store -> enqueue backup/snapshot purge. The live store purge completes within the 30-day SLA window.

- Backups/snapshots: snapshots are immutable once taken and are stored in a dedicated bucket per customer. Snapshots are scheduled for purge based on retention policy; default snapshot retention is 90 days. Purge removes snapshot manifests and associated objects; objects are overwritten or tombstoned depending on underlying storage provider. For customers using customer-managed keys, backups are encrypted with the provided KMS key.

- Log retention and forensic availability: audit/access logs are collected centrally and retained for 180 days (default). We retain two classes of logs: security/audit logs (180 days) and operational metrics logs (90 days). For HIPAA customers we can provide a configurable retention profile (we have customers on 30/90/180-day tiers).

- Verification & evidence: delete job IDs, purge timestamps, and snapshot manifests are available and can be exported as part of a compliance evidence package. If Amaya needs scheduled monthly proof of deletion for records older than X, we can automate periodic reports.

If you want, we can schedule a short 30-minute technical call with our infra team to walk through the purge flow and encryption details.

Regards,
